questions.stem: How does wind increase the rate of transpiration?

options.text: Wind forces open the stomata on the leaf surface
Wind increases the temperature of the leaf
Wind blows away the layer of humid air around the leaf, maintaining a steep concentration gradient
Wind pushes more water up through the xylem from the roots

questions.explanation: In still air, a layer of humid air builds up around the leaf, reducing the concentration gradient. Wind blows this layer away, maintaining a steep gradient so water vapour continues to diffuse out rapidly.
